record.title: CS-MoE reports cross-layer expert sharing with matched-budget perplexity gains through 12B parameters
record.summary: A preprint proposes CS-MoE, which combines layer-local experts with a shared expert pool available across transformer layers. The authors report lower perplexity than dense and layer-isolated MoE baselines under matched parameter and FLOP budgets in Qwen3-backbone experiments spanning 0.6B–12B parameters. At 8B scale, one reported configuration activates 55% of physical parameters per forward pass and reaches perplexity 9.55 versus 9.75 for the dense baseline; this result is not the same as the paper’s separate 4.5-trillion-token downstream comparison. The largest reported models are 12B; routing stability, distributed-system efficiency, and post-training behavior at larger scales remain unestablished.
organizations: China Electronics Cloud Technology Co., Ltd.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors propose CS-MoE, combining layer-specific experts with a shared expert pool accessible across transformer layers.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across Qwen3-backbone experiments from 0.6B to 12B parameters, the authors report lower perplexity than dense baselines under matched parameter and FLOP budgets; one 8B configuration activates 55% of physical parameters and reports perplexity 9.55 versus 9.75 for the 8B dense baseline.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: At matched total-parameter and active-FLOP budgets, the paper reports perplexity 9.65 versus 9.70 at 8B scale and 9.19 versus 9.40 at 12B scale against its layer-isolated sparse-MoE comparisons.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_SCOPE_LIMITATION
claims.text: The inspected paper states that its empirical validation stops at 12B parameters and leaves 70B-plus scaling, distributed acceleration, and post-training pipelines for future study.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the training runs or reported perplexity/downstream results was inspected.
The authors validate through 12B parameters; large-scale routing, training stability, and system performance at 70B-plus remain unmeasured.
The paper does not establish post-training performance or end-to-end serving-cost advantages for CS-MoE.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, cross-layer sharing could change expert-model architecture and parameter-versus-FLOP allocation choices in resource-constrained training. The reported gains are modest in some matched comparisons, limited to experiments through 12B parameters, and do not establish serving-cost or larger-scale benefits.
limitations: All quantitative results are reported by the paper authors and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The reported 55%-active-parameter, 8B perplexity comparison is distinct from the separate 8B downstream benchmark reported after 4.5 trillion training tokens.
The paper’s largest reported model is 12B; performance at 70B-plus, distributed-system gains, and post-training effects remain unknown.
organizations: China Electronics Cloud Technology Co., Ltd.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report matched-budget perplexity gains for CS-MoE relative to dense and layer-isolated sparse-MoE baselines; an 8B setup activates 55% of physical parameters and reports PPL 9.55 versus 9.75 for an 8B dense model.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary source documents the proposed architecture and author-reported experimental results; no result was independently reproduced in this activation.
technical.mechanism: Each transformer layer has local experts and a router-selected subset from a shared expert pool accessible across depth, allowing parameters to be reused at multiple layers.
technical.regime: Author-run Qwen3-backbone experiments from 0.6B to 12B parameters using matched parameter/FLOP comparisons and selected downstream evaluations.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper’s within-study dense and layer-isolated sparse-MoE baselines matched on total parameter footprint and active FLOPs.

brief.title: CS-MoE reports cross-layer expert sharing with matched-budget perplexity gains through 12B parameters
brief.why_it_matters: Cross-layer parameter reuse is a concrete architecture route for trading stored capacity against active computation. If the reported matched-budget gains reproduce, they could affect the design of sparse language models under memory or compute limits.
